condition: H. pylori test-and-treat in a first-degree relative of a gastric cancer patient
permutationLabel: Asymptomatic man aged 44, father had gastric cancer
summary: 44-year-old asymptomatic man whose father died of gastric cancer at 62. Maastricht VI: test first-degree relatives for H. pylori (urea breath test or stool antigen) and treat if positive.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Father had stomach cancer — wants to be checked
inputs.hpi: Asymptomatic 44-year-old man. Father died of gastric adenocarcinoma at 62. No dyspepsia, no dysphagia, no weight loss, no vomiting, no melaena. Not on NSAIDs or PPIs. Never tested for H. pylori.
comorbidities: Family history: father gastric cancer at 62

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Family history of gastric cancer — H. pylori test-and-treat
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Asymptomatic FDR of a gastric cancer patient. Non-invasive H. pylori test (urea breath test or stool antigen, off PPI 2 weeks); eradicate if positive and confirm eradication.

mustInclude.note: Maastricht VI: test-and-treat FDRs of gastric cancer patients.

emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: Over-triage: the chief complaint 'Father had stomach cancer' matches 'Possible malignancy' (priority) and the family-history comorbidity counts as higher-risk → same_day_call (score 37). (The negated alarm symptoms no longer fire.)
emergencyLevel.proposedFix: Treat topic words ('cancer screening', a relative's cancer) as context rather than a current malignancy red flag, and treat 'no change in bowel habit' as negated (the matcher currently handles 'no change' as a pseudo-negation).

mustExclude.note: An ACS, PE or AF antithrombotic/thrombolytic plan must never be attached to this diagnosis. Regression guard for DiagnosisRadiationEngine keyword matching: before 999f838 (word-boundary lookup) the first-substring match would have attached the acute coronary syndrome (aspirin 300 mg, ticagrelor, fondaparinux) plan to this diagnosis because "mi" is inside "family". With word-boundary matching no radiation entry matches (simulated from the source), so iOS is expected to pass; to be confirmed on the first iOS CI run.

guideline.name: Management of Helicobacter pylori infection — the Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report
guideline.section: Test-and-treat for H. pylori in first-degree relatives of patients with gastric cancer; non-invasive testing (urea breath test or monoclonal stool antigen); confirm eradication after treatment
guideline.citation: Malfertheiner P, Megraud F, Rokkas T, et al. Management of Helicobacter pylori infection: the Maastricht VI/Florence consensus report. Gut. 2022;71:1724–1762.

rationale: H. pylori eradication in relatives of gastric cancer patients reduces their gastric cancer risk. Negated alarm symptoms and the word "cancer" in the family history should not escalate the visit.

authoring.author: Claude (prevention/screening, obstetric-gynaecological mimics and paediatric surgery cluster)
authoring.notes: Expectations need surgeon sign-off (reviewedBy). Every citation is verified: false. iOS outcomes are unverified (not run on Linux); triage after the first CI run.
